system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: AWS
G2: GCP
G3: software development
G4: Go beyond terratest

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Filling the 2020-2022 or 2024 gaps with invented jobs or stretching neighbouring date ranges
T2: Disclosing more private/medical detail than needed (father's death) instead of a neutral 'career break' if anything
T3: Claiming AWS or GCP for multi-cloud ads
T4: Calling him a software developer or claiming Python/Go development
T5: Old cover letter targets an IT Administrator job and says 'available to start immediately' - no longer true
T6: The CV lists skills first; writer should keep dates accurate when reordering

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing, building, and operating Azure
environments, including landing-zone network architecture, Terraform infrastructure as code, Azure
DevOps deployment automation, and AKS operations. Experience includes Azure landing-zone
networking, AKS operations, cloud migration, and security automation. Combines systems
administration experience across Windows and Linux with practical infrastructure automation using
PowerShell.
CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Azure IaaS, Azure landing zones, Azure Migrate,
Azure VMs
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Terraform modules, PowerShell, Azure
DevOps YAML pipelines, Go (Terratest tests), Python (small scripts)
Networking and security: Hub-spoke networking, VNets, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private
DNS zones, private endpoints, site-to-site VPN, Microsoft 365 security baselines, Entra ID, MFA,
conditional access
Containers and delivery: AKS operations (upgrades, node pools, ingress), Docker, Helm, App
Service, CI/CD
Systems: Windows and Linux servers, VMware, Proxmox
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics 2025–Present
• Build and maintain Azure landing-zone infrastructure, Terraform modules, and Azure DevOps
pipelines.
• Designed and implemented hub-spoke cloud network architecture in Terraform, including Azure
Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across three
subscriptions.
• Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job.
• Replaced manual deployment processes for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure
DevOps YAML pipelines for build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS.
• Helped increase deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most
applications.
• Operate AKS upgrades, node pools, and ingress; application manifests remain owned by
development teams.
Freelance IT Support 2022–2023
• Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for small-business Microsoft 365 security
baselines.
• Enabled MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing, and backups for small clients.
Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services 2014–2020
• Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers and supported staff across several
municipal services.
• Planned and executed the lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using
Azure Migrate.
• Completed cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
• Used PowerShell to automate infrastructure and administrative tasks.
CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Caregiving and unpaid IT support Mar 2020–Aug 2022
• Left municipal employment to provide full-time care for father; provided unpaid IT help to church
and family during this period.
Independent study and cloud training Feb 2024–Feb 2025
• Studied Terraform and built a Proxmox homelab.
• Completed a three-month, part-time online, English-language cloud bootcamp in Dec 2024.
CERTIFICATIONS
• Microsoft Azure Administrator Associate
• HashiCorp Terraform Associate, 2025

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. The
opportunity to help shape and operate the infrastructure connecting a new train fleet with
cloud services is a strong match for my Azure infrastructure and automation experience.
As a Cloud Engineer at Havenstad Logistics, I design, build and operate Azure landing-zone
infrastructure, Terraform modules (infrastructure as code) and Azure DevOps pipelines. I
designed and implemented a hub-spoke network across three subscriptions, including Azure
Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints and VNet peering. I also added Terratest
module checks and nightly drift detection. For 15 internal applications, I replaced manual
deployments with pipelines for build, test and deployment, helping increase release frequency
from roughly monthly to several times a week for most applications.
Earlier, as a Systems Administrator, I led the migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure
IaaS, planning and executing the cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
Across these roles, I have worked with Windows and Linux systems, networking, and practical
security automation. I also operate AKS upgrades, node pools and ingress, while application
manifests remain owned by development teams. My cloud experience is Azure-focused,
supported by the Microsoft Azure Administrator Associate and HashiCorp Terraform Associate
certifications.
I would welcome the opportunity to apply this experience to Corvale’s fleet connectivity work,
particularly the design, automation and reliable operation of the cloud infrastructure behind
connected services. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how
my background could contribute to the project.
Kind regards,
Samuel Achterberg-Osei

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
